entries.title: DOJ announces extradition and initial appearance of an Israeli national charged over a $2.89 million virtual currency theft from the Nomad Bridge
entries.facts: On 2026-10-30 the U.S. Department of Justice announced, in Office of Public Affairs press release 26-1300, that Alexander Gurevich, 49, an Israeli national, had his initial appearance in the Northern District of California on a 2023 indictment charging him in connection with the theft of $2.89 million in virtual currency from the Nomad Bridge. The release states that he exploited a self-executing computer program, also known as a smart contract, and transferred a total of 103 WBTC (Wrapped Bitcoin) and 300 WETH (Wrapped Ether), with an estimated value of approximately $2,894,390 at the time of the transactions, and that he is alleged to have laundered the proceeds through conversions and transfers to conceal and disguise them. Gurevich is charged with causing damage to a protected computer, interstate transportation of stolen money, and money laundering. The release states that he was arrested in Israel in May 2025 and was recently extradited, and that if convicted he faces a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine for causing damage to a protected computer, as well as for interstate transportation of stolen money, and 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine for money laundering. The Department states that an indictment is merely an allegation and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
entries.source_label: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs, Press Release 26-1300 (October 30, 2026)
